1|# How the Rork Proxy Works
     2|
     3|The Rork Toolkit server (`EXPO_PUBLIC_TOOLKIT_URL`, e.g. `toolkit.rork.com`) acts as a **reverse proxy** that forwards AI requests to upstream providers. It handles authentication, billing, rate limiting, and cost tracking so that the generated app only needs a single API key.
     4|
     5|## URL structure
     6|
     7|```
     8|${TOOLKIT_URL}/v2/<service>/<upstream-path>
     9|```
    10|
    11|The proxy strips the `/v2/<service>` prefix and forwards the **rest of the path as-is** to the upstream.
    12|
    13|- `/v2/vercel/` → Vercel AI Gateway (`ai-gateway.vercel.sh`). Example: `/v2/vercel/v1/chat/completions` → `ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/chat/completions`. Gateway speech uses `/v2/vercel/v4/ai/speech-model`; Gateway transcription uses `/v2/vercel/v4/ai/transcription-model`.
    14|- `/v2/elevenlabs/` → ElevenLabs. Example: `/v2/elevenlabs/v1/text-to-speech/...` or `/v2/elevenlabs/v1/speech-to-text`.
    15|- `/v2/exa/` → Exa (`api.exa.ai`). Example: `/v2/exa/search` → `api.exa.ai/search`.
    16|
    17|**The upstream path must be complete and correct**, including version prefixes like `/v1/`, `/v3/ai/`, or `/v4/ai/`. Omitting them (e.g. `/v2/vercel/chat/completions` instead of `/v2/vercel/v1/chat/completions`) will result in a **404** from the upstream.
    18|
    19|## Authentication
    20|
    21|Browser builds (standalone web and React Native web preview) receive
    22|short-lived delegated authentication from the Rork build runtime. Do not mint,
    23|store, return, or manually expose `EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_TOOLKIT_SECRET_KEY` to
    24|browser code. Calls to `EXPO_PUBLIC_TOOLKIT_URL` may omit `Authorization`; the
    25|runtime injects the delegated bearer token. Existing cross-platform React
    26|Native source may still set the legacy header: web builds replace the value
    27|with a non-secret placeholder and the runtime overwrites it before transport.
    28|
    29|Native and server-only calls continue to include:
    30|
    31|```
    32|Authorization: Bearer <EXPO_PUBLIC_RORK_TOOLKIT_SECRET_KEY>
    33|Content-Type: application/json
    34|```
    35|
    36|Rork AI Cloud is enabled by calling the `getOrCreateToolkitSecret` tool with a
    37|short description of why the app needs it. The tool checks Cloud Credits
    38|status without exposing the value. If Cloud Credits are already enabled,
    39|continue without asking. Only ask the user to enable or claim credits when the
    40|tool returns confirmation required.
    41|
    42|## Base URL
    43|
    44|The base URL is available as the environment variable `EXPO_PUBLIC_TOOLKIT_URL`.

(End of file - total 44 lines)

1|# Live model discovery
     2|
     3|Treat remembered model IDs as stale. Before writing any model ID, including fallbacks, refresh the Vercel catalog:
     4|
     5|```sh
     6|catalog_dir="$(mktemp -d /tmp/rork-models.XXXXXX)"
     7|curl -fsS https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models -o "$catalog_dir/vercel-models.json.tmp"
     8|jq -e '.data | type == "array"' "$catalog_dir/vercel-models.json.tmp" >/dev/null
     9|mv "$catalog_dir/vercel-models.json.tmp" "$catalog_dir/vercel-models.json"
    10|```
    11|
    12|Keep using this run's `$catalog_dir`. Filter with `jq` or `rg`; never print the whole catalog.
    13|
    14|## Selection flow
    15|
    16|1. Filter `.data` by `owned_by`, `type`, `tags`, or `modalities`, then sort for the task.
    17|2. When cost or capability tradeoffs are material, present the candidate and alternatives before implementation. Do not pause for an explicit or obvious choice.
    18|3. Fetch the chosen model's endpoint metadata:
    19|
    20|   ```sh
    21|   model_id='provider/model'
    22|   curl -fsS "https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/v1/models/$model_id/endpoints" \
    23|     -o "$catalog_dir/vercel-model-endpoints.json.tmp"
    24|   jq -e '.data.endpoints | type == "array"' "$catalog_dir/vercel-model-endpoints.json.tmp" >/dev/null
    25|   mv "$catalog_dir/vercel-model-endpoints.json.tmp" "$catalog_dir/vercel-model-endpoints.json"
    26|   jq '.data' "$catalog_dir/vercel-model-endpoints.json"
    27|   ```
    28|
    29|4. Treat the endpoint response as authoritative for modalities, limits, parameters, pricing, provider options, and request shape. If it is missing, choose again instead of guessing.
    30|5. Report the selected model ID and reason in the final summary.
    31|
    32|For image generation, match the `image-generation` tag or an `image` output modality, then route by `type`: language models use chat completions; image models use `/v3/ai/image-model`. Video models use `/v3/ai/video-model`, embeddings use `/v1/embeddings`, and other language models use `/v1/chat/completions`.

(End of file - total 32 lines)
